title: Poisoning
description: Swallowing, inhaling, or absorbing a harmful substance — chemicals, medications, pesticides, generator fumes, contaminated food, or alcohol.

recognition_questions.q: What substance, how much, and when? (Look for containers.)
Is the person drowsy, confused, or unconscious?
Are they vomiting or having difficulty breathing?

immediate_safety_warnings: Do NOT make the person vomit — some substances cause more damage coming back up.
Do not give anything by mouth if the person is drowsy or unconscious.
Move the person away from the source (fumes, spilled chemical) before helping.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Call 112 immediately, or the nearest poison control centre if available.
Move the person away from the poison source (e.g. out of a room with generator fumes).
Take the container, bottle, or remaining substance to hospital or give to emergency services.
ordered_instructions.rationale: Identifies the poison so the right treatment can be given.

ordered_instructions.instruction: If the person is conscious and breathing, keep them awake and on their side in the recovery position.
ordered_instructions.rationale: Protects the airway if they vomit.

ordered_instructions.instruction: If the person is unconscious but breathing, place in recovery position and monitor.
If unconscious and not breathing, start CPR.

actions_to_avoid: Do not give milk, water, or any 'antidote' unless told to by poison control.
Do not give activated charcoal unless directed by a professional.
Do not put your face near a chemical spill to smell it.

escalation_conditions.condition: Person is unconscious, drowsy, or confused

escalation_conditions.action: Move to fresh air immediately; call 112; suspect CO poisoning
Remove contaminated clothing; flush skin with water for 20 minutes
Flush eye with running water for 20 minutes, holding eyelid open

follow_up_requirements: All poisoning needs hospital assessment, even if the person seems well initially.

age_specific_pathways.child: Children are more sensitive to small doses — seek urgent care for any suspected poisoning.
age_specific_pathways.infant: Any suspected poisoning in an infant is an emergency.

source_references.document: International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines
